reviewScope: DR-125 component-sdk-contract v1 only. This review does not mark DR-125 SATISFIED, qualify or demonstrate anything, authorize docs/v2/implementation/, or apply or seal the candidate.
summary: REJECT. The candidate preserves the exact file-02 developer text and unique live DR-125 row, chooses no SDK API/framework, mints no D9/exit value, does not rewrite DR-102 bytes, keeps capability tokens host-owned, and makes no SATISFIED, QUALIFIED, G20-authorship, or implementation-authorization claim. Acceptance is nevertheless barred by CSCV1-B1: T-1 merely promotes CPC's already-pending ownership split without defining the host trigger, mandatory applied-provider Cancel transition, carrier-to-carrier reachability/order, terminal exceptions, or an executable G20 trace; CPC-only cancellation therefore remains conforming to the written candidate even though it starves the controlling TypeScript in-band path. CSCV1-S1 additionally records a stale coordinator digest and a D-015 routing attribution absent from that source. At 1 blocker and 1 SHOULD-FIX, DR-125 remains OPEN and this verdict authorizes nothing.

blockers.title: T-1 assigns the two carriers to different owners but never composes their required transitions
blockers.measurement: The candidate's two split clauses and J-1 sentence restate control-protocol-contract.v2 tensionsObserved.items[T-1].pendingResolutionThisCandidate almost exactly: supervision-scoped control cancel, provider-side ownership of in-band Cancel, and J-1 ordering only. The accepted CPC itself labels that text pending. The applied TypeScript contract is stronger: providerProtocol.ordering.cancelTransition permits Cancel once from any nonterminal state and requires Cancelled then EOF, while supervision.userCancellation requires SIGINT/SIGTERM before finalization to send Cancel once, close the request side, wait the bounded cleanup grace, then terminate if needed. The live DR-102 row routes T-1 to DR-125 'with the applied TS contract's in-band `Cancel` controlling.' The candidate contains no rule saying an applicable host cancellation dispatches both participants, no MUST for the provider-side participant to execute the applicable in-band transition, and no ordering/fence preventing CPC teardown from making that transition unreachable. CPC J-1 orders the supervision cancel against a provider result; it does not order the supervision cancel against the provider Cancel. The named G20 golden consequently has two stimuli but no expected composite trace.
blockers.counterexample: A host can satisfy the written split by emitting only the CPC supervision cancel while leaving the in-band frame merely 'owned' by a provider-side participant that is never invoked. Alternatively it can emit CPC cancel first, allow the component to exit on the teardown announcement, and only then attempt provider Cancel. Both implementations obey the two ownership sentences and the no-control-plane-authoring rule, yet both starve the applied provider cancellation path that the candidate says cannot be dropped.
blockers.whyBlocker: Resolving the dual-carrier tension is the candidate's stated purpose. Renaming CPC's pending split as ACCEPTED without a trigger, provider-transition obligation, or reachability ordering does not decide how the carriers compose and cannot supply an executable G20 oracle. DR-125 therefore still lacks the T-1 contract it claims to provide.
blockers.requiredRepair: Specify the composition at behavior-contract level without choosing an SDK API: identify which host cancellation events require dual-carrier fanout and how other causes branch; require the owning provider-side participant, when the applied provider protocol has a live in-band cancellation transition, to execute that transition exactly as that protocol requires; state that this in-band path controls provider semantics and is not replaced by CPC cancel; and constrain supervisory teardown so it cannot close, kill, or otherwise preclude the required provider transition before that transition is committed or a named already-terminal/unavailable condition is established. Preserve CPC's separate supervision-only cancel and J-1/J-5 authority. Give G20 positive and negative traces with a determinate expected order/outcome, including the no-in-band-cancel provider case and already-terminal/faulted cases. Mint no frame, payload, fate, D9, exit, API, or framework here.
